## Decision29 amendment: explicit coarse-clock evidence for the CI denial join

Context: see the original retained A/B CI diagnostics and proposal. Both original host-facts records identify6.17.0-1022-azure. The B audit MESSAGE time is2.187040ms earlier than its unshare start, exceeding the current2ms allowance; journal reception realtime and monotonic comparisons pass. A matches the original join. No B test suite/profile load occurred. The preliminary301257ns journal-realtime lag is a real observation but is not the rejecting predicate; retain its explicit dispatch addendum.

Upstream Linuxv6.17 [audit.c](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.17/kernel/audit.c#L1724) uses a coarse realtime stamp when no syscall-context stamp is available and formats milliseconds by integer division; [auditsc.c](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.17/kernel/auditsc.c#L1905) also samples coarse realtime at syscall entry. [The documented coarse accessor](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v6.17/core-api/timekeeping.html#coarse-and-fast-ns-access) corresponds to userspace CLOCK_REALTIME_COARSE and reflects the last timer tick. [LinuxUAPI](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.17/include/uapi/linux/time.h#L43) defines clockid5. [systemd's journal field definitions](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v255/man/systemd.journal-fields.xml) distinguish reception realtime/monotonic from message origin. These sources justify the clock design; they do not attest the exact patched running kernel/systemd binary or retrospectively establish B's unrecorded coarse samples.

The new original_ready record declares a distinct namespace clock contract version. The live consumer supplies an expected new version from its trusted known producer/capture source context; it never infers permission to use legacy from absence in an untrusted record. Explicit historical or pure callers may select the legacy contract. In the new contract, take one available-or-unavailable CLOCK_REALTIME_COARSE sample before the original unshare observation starts and one after the original failed /proc/self/setgroups open's existing terminal timestamps are obtained. Each available sample carries exact non-bool integer nanoseconds, clockid5/name, phase, original PID/boot and monotonic sampling start/end. The monotonic order must prove that these observations enclose the unchanged original operations, inside the original capture and job interval. Retain an actual capture terminal-monotonic field; no deadline is reset. Sampling errors remain explicit unavailable facts and cannot mask or replace the original syscall result/exception, trigger a second call, or create a thread. Cancellation exceptions propagate. Restrict added observations to this admitted denial sequence and preserve original byte/row/report limits.

For the expected new contract, floor the two observed coarse endpoints to1ms and require the unchanged audit MESSAGE millisecond timestamp to lie inclusively between them. Equal endpoints are valid. Removing both sample fields and the record declaration still fails the live expected-new join; partial/unknown-version/unavailable/foreign/malformed/reversed/outside-capture observations fail before privileged profile operations. Preserve all original joins and the existing journal reception realtime/monotonic guards. Only expressly selected genuinely legacy records lacking the new contract and fields use the original strict2ms audit-wall predicate; original B remains failed. Return the actual clock basis and endpoints as nonauthorizing join evidence. Live clock resolution is unnecessary for this same-clock-bin join and must not generate a tolerance.

A larger guessed fine-clock tolerance or dropping the audit check would obscure clock semantics and is rejected. The measured bracket preserves explicit original clock provenance; missing/late facts intentionally still fail CI. Focused portable tests must prove coarse lag over2ms can join only with genuine-format valid sample fixtures, equal/boundary bins, foreign/missing/partial/malformed/reversed/unknown/unavailable/out-of-bracket rejection, original journal guards, legacy B rejection and original delegate-once/error precedence. Fixtures are not real policy denials or profile authority. Current exact-source hosted and ext4 complete portable/native/source/skip checks remain mandatory. CI-only paths are outside the actually observed selected95; preserve source/image scientific authority and immutable current CPU/GPU results after explicit final source-impact proof.
